methods.label: Choose one point first
methods.explanation:
Choosing one point first helps because every marked point has the same number of unit-distance neighbors.

The marked points are the four corners and four side midpoints. Each corner is one unit from the two midpoints next to it, and each side midpoint is one unit from that side's two corners. Midpoints of adjacent sides are \(\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt2>1\) units apart by the Pythagorean theorem. Every other nonneighboring pair spans at least two units horizontally or vertically. Thus each point has exactly two unit-distance neighbors.

Imagine choosing the first point uniformly from the eight points, then choosing the second uniformly from the seven remaining points. Every unordered pair arises in exactly two orders, so all pairs still have the same chance. Whichever point comes first, two of the seven possible second points are favorable. Therefore the probability is
\[
\boxed{\frac{2}{7}},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
